finding.claim: With the verifier cache enabled, a token that carries `exp` but no numeric `iat` is cached with an expiry of the full `cacheTTL` (default 10 minutes) rather than its own `exp`. The token keeps verifying successfully from the cache after it has expired. The `exp` and `nbf` bounds are only recorded inside `if (hasIat)`.
finding.source: A validly signed token whose payload has `exp` but no `iat`, for example one issued with the signer's `noTimestamp: true` and `expiresIn`, or by another issuer that omits `iat`. The verifier must be created with `cache` enabled. The holder of such a token is the attacker, and they replay it after `exp`.
finding.sink: The cache-hit branch in `verify()` returns the cached payload without re-running `verifyToken`, so `exp` is never checked and an expired token is accepted as authenticated.

trace.note: A successful verification calls cacheSet(cacheContext, payload).
hasIat is false because payload.iat is not a number.
The block that sets cacheValue[1] (nbf) and cacheValue[2] (exp) is skipped, so cacheValue[2] stays 0.
cacheValue[2] === 0 is replaced by maxTTL, so the entry is valid for cacheTTL regardless of exp.
A later call with the same token reads the cache entry.
The hit test passes: min === 0 and now <= max, so the expiry check is bypassed.
The cached payload is returned without calling verifyToken, so the exp validator at line 304 never runs.

finding.guards_checked: The `exp` validator in `verifyToken` (lines 304-323) only runs on a cache miss. The cache-hit check at lines 368-375 uses only the cached min/max, and max is wrong in this case. `requiredClaims` is opt-in and does not require `iat` by default. `maxAge` has no effect on this path because the entry stores no iat-derived bound. The signature is genuinely valid, so no other control rejects the token. The exposure is bounded by `cacheTTL`; setting `cache: false` or requiring `iat` avoids it.
